Okay, let's imagine you and your friends are playing outside, and two toy airplanes are flying in the sky above you. Sometimes, in real life, big airplanes (called fighter planes) chase each other in the sky during a war. They shoot little metal things called bullets at each other.

Now, when these bullets fly through the air, they might hit the ground. Also, sometimes the planes drop things called bombs or shells, and when those explode in the air, pieces and fire can fall down. This is called "falling flak" or "falling debris."

All of this—bullets hitting the ground, explosions in the sky, or even a plane falling down—can hurt people or animals on the ground who are not soldiers. These people are called "civilians." Sometimes, soldiers on the ground can also get hurt.

But it's really hard to know exactly how many people get hurt this way, because it depends on where the fighting happens, how long it goes on, and how close the fighting is to where people live.

So, when people ask how many people get hurt on the ground from these air fights, it's a tricky question and there isn't always a clear number. But yes, sometimes people and animals on the ground can get hurt when there are big air battles above them.
